assertions.name: scale_absorbs_multiplicative_factor
assertions.source: ln A and (1/2)ln A are the same hypothesis once the scale constant is free, so they must score identically. A self-check on the scoring, not a result.

assertions.name: geometric_consistency_costs_fit
assertions.source: Hyperbolic-consistent ln A scores 9.253% against the imported A^(1/3) at 3.505%, a factor 2.64.

assertions.name: data_prefers_the_euclidean_exponent
assertions.source: Free-power optimum p = 0.33 against the Euclidean 1/3. Diagnostic with one extra DOF; recorded as a boolean so a future run that moves it fails loudly.

description: Provenance and self-consistency check on the separation law alpha(A) that every kernel hypothesis on this front is fed. The law alpha ~ A^(1/3) is imported by em_linking_coth_separation_probe.py as 'the standard nuclear radius law' -- a Euclidean liquid-drop result -- while the kernel it feeds is hyperbolic ('coth is forced by the Green's function'). This scores the geometrically self-consistent alternative (H^3 volume growth gives R ~ (1/2)ln V, so alpha ~ ln A for extensive V) against the imported one on the same series with the same statistic.

the_import.quoted_justification: '(3) A^(1/3) was fixed in advance as the standard nuclear radius law, not selected post hoc.' -- em_linking_coth_separation_probe.py, honest_caveats
the_import.what_that_establishes: Protection against post-hoc selection, which is real and worth having.
the_import.what_it_does_not_establish: That the law is derived. A^(1/3) is the Euclidean liquid-drop nuclear radius; it is imported phenomenology, not framework output.
the_import.the_straddle: The same file states the kernel has 'NO free parameter -- coth is forced by the Green's function', i.e. the kernel is hyperbolic by construction. Feeding a Euclidean size law into a hyperbolic kernel mixes two geometries inside one quantity.

what_the_geometry_requires.fact: In H^3 a ball of radius R has volume pi(sinh 2R - 2R) ~ (pi/2)e^(2R), so R ~ (1/2)ln(2V/pi).
what_the_geometry_requires.consequence: For extensive volume V ~ A the hyperbolic separation scale grows like ln A, not A^(1/3).
what_the_geometry_requires.caveat: V ~ A is itself an assumption. The corpus cannot check it: see corpus_cannot_settle_it below.

cost_of_geometric_self_consistency.reading: Using the geometry consistently costs a factor 2.64 in scatter. So H_coth's fit quality depends on the geometric mixture, not on the hyperbolic kernel alone.

corpus_cannot_settle_it.available: binding-link-volumes.witness.json carries hyperbolic link volumes for A = 2 and A = 3 only: Hopf (0, Seifert-fibred), 8_11 (8.2863), L6a4 (7.3277).
corpus_cannot_settle_it.its_own_verdict: 'the A-dependence is not in a single binding-link volume' -- that witness's description.
corpus_cannot_settle_it.consequence: There is no per-isotope hyperbolic geometry in the corpus beyond A = 3, so no alpha(A) law can currently be DERIVED from framework data. Whatever law is used on this front is imported from outside it.

preferred_power_DIAGNOSTIC.DOF_WARNING: This scan is a fit with one more DOF than any fixed-p hypothesis. It is a diagnostic, never support.
preferred_power_DIAGNOSTIC.reading: The optimum sits essentially ON the Euclidean exponent, and its scatter is indistinguishable from the p = 1/3 value, so the data is consistent with exactly 1/3 and does not resolve a different power. The data independently prefers the Euclidean nuclear radius law.

deflationary_reading.claim: The kappa(A) profile is close to what plain Coulomb repulsion in a Euclidean nucleus of radius R ~ A^(1/3) gives, with the hyperbolic kernel contributing a small curvature correction.
deflationary_reading.calibration: The curvature term does buy something real -- 5.499% falls to 3.505% for one shared parameter. But a factor 1.57 in scatter is suggestive, not decisive, and is comparable to what the frozen-B_pp confound (qou-gcmn) could account for on its own.
deflationary_reading.NOT_claimed: That the geometry is Euclidean, that there is no hyperbolic content, or that H_coth is refuted. The measured range does not resolve the question; that is the point.

scope.class: (a) scope-limited negative on an INPUT ASSUMPTION shared by every hypothesis on this front
scope.what_is_claimed: alpha ~ A^(1/3) is imported Euclidean phenomenology, not derived; the framework carries no data from which to derive a rival; and geometric self-consistency costs 2.64x in fit.
scope.what_is_NOT_claimed: That A^(1/3) is wrong. The data prefers it. What is claimed is that its warrant is phenomenological rather than framework-derived, and that this has not been stated.

data.verdict: The separation law every kernel on this front is fed, alpha ~ A^(1/3), is the EUCLIDEAN liquid-drop nuclear radius, imported and labelled 'fixed in advance' -- which guards against post-hoc selection but is not derivation. The kernel it feeds is hyperbolic by construction, so the two mix geometries. Scored on the same series: the imported law gives 3.505% scatter, the geometrically self-consistent ln A law gives 9.253% -- consistency costs 2.64x. The corpus cannot adjudicate: it carries hyperbolic link volumes at A = 2 and 3 only. A free-power diagnostic lands at p = 0.33, indistinguishable from 1/3, so the data independently prefers the Euclidean exponent. Deflationary reading, stated plainly: kappa(A) is close to plain Coulomb in a Euclidean nucleus (5.499% for the pure 1/r law), with the hyperbolic curvature term worth a factor 1.57 on one shared parameter -- suggestive, not decisive, and comparable to the frozen-B_pp confound. Nothing here refutes H_coth; what it removes is the impression that the hyperbolic reading was ever load-bearing for the fit.
